# Daag (দাগ)

> A verified public archive documenting misogynistic, victim-blaming and abusive
> comments posted on social media about gender violence in Bangladesh. Every
> entry is a real comment by a named account, kept with a screenshot, a link to
> the source post, and a category, and published only after a human moderator
> has reviewed it.

Daag is run as a non-commercial public-interest archive. Site language is
Bengali by default, with English available. Contact: daagarchive@gmail.com

## What the archive is

- Entries record what someone publicly wrote underneath reporting about gender
  violence. They do not record the underlying crime, and Daag does not
  investigate incidents.
- Nothing is published without a screenshot. An entry cannot be approved
  without one.
- Submitter identity is never published. The person named in an entry cannot
  see who reported them.
- Anyone named in an entry can appeal. A moderator other than the one who
  approved it reviews the evidence within 14 working days, and the outcome and
  reason are recorded.

## What it is not

Daag is a record, not a verdict and not a punishment. It takes no position on
guilt in any criminal matter, publishes no private data, and asks that entries
not be used to harass anyone. Using it to organise abuse against a person is
against its terms.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.daag-bd.com/): what the archive is and how to search it
- [The Record](https://www.daag-bd.com/archive): every published entry, filterable by category, incident type and severity
- [Profile Search](https://www.daag-bd.com/search): look up a name or profile link
- [Submit Evidence](https://www.daag-bd.com/submit): report a publicly posted comment
- [Appeals](https://www.daag-bd.com/appeals): dispute an entry, or track an appeal already filed
- [Analysis](https://www.daag-bd.com/analytics): categories, incident types and how the record has grown
- [About](https://www.daag-bd.com/about): why the archive exists, the rules it holds itself to, and answers to common questions
- [Terms of Use](https://www.daag-bd.com/terms)
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.daag-bd.com/privacy)
- [Contact](https://www.daag-bd.com/contact)

## Citing Daag

Cite entries by their reference number, for example DG-2025-5370, together with
the archive name. Figures shown on the Analysis page are computed from Daag's
own database and are current as of the time of reading. Do not reproduce the
archived comments in full as though they were Daag's own words: they are quoted
evidence of what another person wrote.
